_note: Generated from verified evidence; see tools/README.md. Counts are rows in the raw source files.

entries.title: Spaces before and after customer names
entries.rows_note: 17 first names and 22 last names carry a leading or trailing space; 29 rows in total.
entries.wrong: The CRM export stores names with stray spaces: row 1 is “ Jon”, “Yang ”. Nothing about the value looks wrong in a table view.
entries.impact: “ Jon” and “Jon” are different strings. They split a GROUP BY, fail an equality join and sort apart from each other.

fixes.text: TRIM() on both name columns in the Silver load.
fixes.code:
TRIM(cst_firstname) AS cst_firstname,
TRIM(cst_lastname) AS cst_lastname,

fixes.text: Trims every string column of the table in one loop, not just the ones known to be dirty.

test.note: The repository’s whitespace check runs on cst_key; the name columns are trimmed on every load.
test.sql:

-- Expectation: No Results
SELECT 
    cst_key 
FROM silver.crm_cust_info
WHERE cst_key != TRIM(cst_key);

entries.title: One customer, two records
entries.rows_note: 5 customer IDs appear more than once: 6 extra rows.
entries.wrong: Some customers were exported twice. For ID 29433 the first copy has no name at all; the second, two days newer, is complete.
entries.impact: A duplicate key in a dimension doubles every fact row that joins to it.

fixes.text: Number each customer’s records by create date, newest first, and keep only the first.
fixes.code:
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cst_id ORDER BY cst_create_date DESC) AS flag_last
...
WHERE flag_last = 1; -- Select the most recent record per customer

entries.title: Marital status stored as one-letter codes
entries.wrong: The CRM stores marital status as M and S, and leaves seven rows empty.
entries.impact: Codes are fine inside one system. In a warehouse that joins two systems, everybody reading the table has to know what they mean.

fixes.text: Mapped to readable values; anything else becomes n/a.
fixes.code:
WHEN UPPER(TRIM(cst_marital_status)) = 'S' THEN 'Single'
WHEN UPPER(TRIM(cst_marital_status)) = 'M' THEN 'Married'
ELSE 'n/a'

fixes.text: Same mapping in PySpark.
fixes.code:
F.when(F.upper(F.col("cst_marital_status")) == "S", "Single")
 .when(F.upper(F.col("cst_marital_status")) == "M", "Married")
 .otherwise("n/a")

test.note: A consistency review rather than a pass/fail check:
test.sql:
-- Data Standardization & Consistency
SELECT DISTINCT 
    cst_marital_status 
FROM silver.crm_cust_info;

entries.title: Gender missing in a quarter of CRM customers
entries.wrong: 4,578 CRM customers have no gender. The ERP file CUST_AZ12 has its own gender column for the same customers.
entries.impact: Two systems disagree or have gaps; the model has to decide which one wins, and say so.

fixes.text: Silver maps M/F to Male/Female. Gold treats the CRM as the primary source and falls back to the ERP when the CRM says n/a.
fixes.code:
WHEN ci.cst_gndr != 'n/a' THEN ci.cst_gndr -- CRM is the primary source for gender
ELSE COALESCE(ca.gen, 'n/a')  			   -- Fallback to ERP data

fixes.text: The same precedence rule in the Gold notebook.
fixes.code:
CASE
    WHEN ci.gender <> 'n/a' THEN ci.gender
    ELSE COALESCE(ca.gender, 'n/a')
END AS gender,

entries.title: Two keys packed into one product key

parts: cat_id — joins the ERP category table

entries.wrong: The first five characters of every product key are a category code, written with a hyphen where the ERP category table uses an underscore.
entries.impact: Without splitting the key, products can’t be joined to their category, and sales can’t be joined to products.

fixes.text: Split into two columns and align the separator with the ERP.
fixes.code:
REPLACE(SUBSTRING(prd_key, 1, 5), '-', '_') AS cat_id, -- Extract category ID
SUBSTRING(prd_key, 7, LEN(prd_key)) AS prd_key,        -- Extract product key

fixes.text: Same split in PySpark.
fixes.code:
df = df.withColumn("cat_id", F.regexp_replace(F.substring(col("prd_key"), 1, 5), "-", "_"))
df = df.withColumn("prd_key", F.substring(col("prd_key"), 7, F.length(col("prd_key"))))

entries.title: Product line codes with a trailing space
entries.wrong: Every product line code is one letter followed by a space; 17 products have none.
entries.impact: A comparison with 'R' fails on 'R '. The space is invisible in most tools.

fixes.text: Trim, upper-case, then map each code to its name.
fixes.code:
WHEN UPPER(TRIM(prd_line)) = 'M' THEN 'Mountain'
WHEN UPPER(TRIM(prd_line)) = 'R' THEN 'Road'
WHEN UPPER(TRIM(prd_line)) = 'S' THEN 'Other Sales'
WHEN UPPER(TRIM(prd_line)) = 'T' THEN 'Touring'
ELSE 'n/a'

fixes.text: Trimmed by the all-columns loop, then mapped.
fixes.code:
F.when(F.upper(col("prd_line")) == "M", "Mountain")
 .when(F.upper(col("prd_line")) == "R", "Road")

entries.title: Products that end before they start
entries.wrong: Half of the product history rows have an end date earlier than their start date.
entries.impact: Product history (which price applied when) can’t be trusted if a version ends before it begins.

fixes.text: Ignore the stored end date. Rebuild it as the day before the next version of the same product starts.
fixes.code:
CAST(
    LEAD(prd_start_dt) OVER (PARTITION BY prd_key ORDER BY prd_start_dt) - 1 
    AS DATE
) AS prd_end_dt -- Calculate end date as one day before the next start date

entries.title: Order dates stored as integers — some of them not dates
entries.rows_note: All 60,398 order dates are integers. 19 can’t be dates at all: 17 zeros, plus 32154 and 5489.
entries.wrong: Order, ship and due dates arrive as eight-digit integers. Nineteen order dates are 0 or have the wrong number of digits.
entries.impact: Integer dates can’t be filtered by month or compared with real dates; casting a bad one fails the whole load.

fixes.text: Invalid values become NULL; the rest are cast through text to DATE.
fixes.code:
CASE 
    WHEN sls_order_dt = 0 OR LEN(sls_order_dt) != 8 THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(CAST(sls_order_dt AS VARCHAR) AS DATE)
END AS sls_order_dt,

fixes.text: Same rule with an explicit yyyyMMdd pattern.
fixes.code:
F.when(
    (col("sls_order_dt") == 0) | (length(col("sls_order_dt")) != 8),
    None
).otherwise(F.to_date(col("sls_order_dt").cast("string"), "yyyyMMdd"))

test.note: The same rule as a check on the raw table:
test.sql:
-- Check for Invalid Dates
-- Expectation: No Invalid Dates
SELECT 
    NULLIF(sls_due_dt, 0) AS sls_due_dt 
FROM bronze.crm_sales_details
WHERE sls_due_dt <= 0 
    OR LEN(sls_due_dt) != 8 
    OR sls_due_dt > 20500101 
    OR sls_due_dt < 19000101;

entries.title: Sales amounts that don’t equal quantity × price
entries.rows_note: 23 rows where the amount is missing, zero or negative, or doesn’t equal quantity × price.
entries.wrong: The sales amount is sometimes missing, negative, or simply doesn’t match the quantity and price on the same line.
entries.impact: Revenue is the number every report starts from. If the line total and its parts disagree, one of them is wrong.

fixes.text: When the amount is missing, not positive or inconsistent, recompute it from quantity × |price|.
fixes.code:
WHEN sls_sales IS NULL OR sls_sales <= 0 OR sls_sales != sls_quantity * ABS(sls_price) 
	THEN sls_quantity * ABS(sls_price)
ELSE sls_sales

test.sql:
-- Check Data Consistency: Sales = Quantity * Price
-- Expectation: No Results
SELECT DISTINCT 
    sls_sales,
    sls_quantity,
    sls_price 
FROM silver.crm_sales_details
WHERE sls_sales != sls_quantity * sls_price
   OR sls_sales IS NULL 
   OR sls_quantity IS NULL 
   OR sls_price IS NULL
   OR sls_sales <= 0 
   OR sls_quantity <= 0 
   OR sls_price <= 0
ORDER BY sls_sales, sls_quantity, sls_price;

entries.title: Prices missing or negative
entries.rows_note: 12 prices are empty, zero or negative (5 negative).
entries.wrong: Twelve sale lines have no usable unit price.
entries.impact: Price feeds every average-price and margin figure; a negative one flips the sign of whatever it touches.

fixes.text: Derive the price from the line total.
fixes.code:
WHEN sls_price IS NULL OR sls_price <= 0 
	THEN sls_sales / NULLIF(sls_quantity, 0)
ELSE sls_price  -- Derive price if original value is invalid

fixes.text: Same derivation in PySpark, guarding against a zero quantity.
fixes.code:
F.when(
    (col("sls_price").isNull()) | (col("sls_price") <= 0),
    F.when(
        col("sls_quantity") != 0,
        col("sls_sales") / col("sls_quantity")
    ).otherwise(None)
).otherwise(col("sls_price"))

entries.title: ERP customer keys with a three-letter prefix
entries.wrong: The ERP writes the same customer number as the CRM, but 11,042 of them start with NAS.
entries.impact: The ERP’s birth dates and genders can’t be joined to CRM customers until the keys match.

fixes.text: Strip the prefix when present.
fixes.code:
WHEN cid LIKE 'NAS%' THEN SUBSTRING(cid, 4, LEN(cid)) -- Remove 'NAS' prefix if present
ELSE cid

fixes.text: Same rule in PySpark.
fixes.code:
F.when(col("cid").startswith("NAS"),
       F.substring(col("cid"), 4, F.length(col("cid"))))
 .otherwise(col("cid"))

entries.title: Customers born in the future
entries.rows_note: 16 birth dates lie in the future, from 2038 to 9999.
entries.wrong: Sixteen ERP birth dates are in the future; four of them are in the year 9999.
entries.impact: A single impossible birth date wrecks an age distribution and any “average age” figure.

fixes.text: Birth dates after today become NULL.
fixes.code:
WHEN bdate > GETDATE() THEN NULL
ELSE bdate

fixes.text: Same rule in PySpark.
fixes.code:
F.when(col("bdate") > F.current_date(), None)
 .otherwise(col("bdate"))

entries.wrong: The ERP gender column mixes full words, single letters, letters with a trailing space, and values that are only spaces.

entries.title: A hyphen in every location key
entries.wrong: The location file writes customer numbers with a hyphen the other two files don’t use.

fixes.text: Remove the hyphen.

entries.title: One country, three spellings
entries.rows_note: 2,591 USA, 1,500 US, 566 DE, 332 empty and 5 made only of spaces.
entries.wrong: Country names are mixed with ISO-style codes, and some values are empty or only spaces.
entries.impact: Sales by country would show the United States three times.

fixes.text: Map codes to names; empty or blank becomes n/a.
fixes.code:
WHEN TRIM(cntry) = 'DE' THEN 'Germany'
WHEN TRIM(cntry) IN ('US', 'USA') THEN 'United States'
WHEN TRIM(cntry) = '' OR cntry IS NULL THEN 'n/a'
ELSE TRIM(cntry)

fixes.text: Same mapping in PySpark.
fixes.code:
F.when(col("cntry") == "DE", "Germany")
 .when(col("cntry").isin("US", "USA"), "United States")
 .when((col("cntry") == "") | col("cntry").isNull(), "n/a")
 .otherwise(col("cntry"))

    billing
    .withColumn(
        "insurance_paid",
        F.round(F.col("insurance_paid"), 2)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "patient_paid",
        F.round(F.col("patient_paid"), 2)
    )
)
